newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks information on N.Korea spy claims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks information on N.Korea spy claims.

text.p: The United States asked Sweden on Sunday to help gather information about North Korea's allegations they had arrested an American for spying, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
"We are aware of the reports," McCurry told Reuters shortly before President Bill Clinton left for Hartford, Connecticut.
"The charge (d'affaires) of the Swedish embassy in Pyongyang is making inquiries on behalf of the United States on the status of this individual," he added.
The Swedish charge d'affaires represents U.S. interests in Pyongyang, which has no diplomatic relations with the United States.
Earlier in the day the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said Evan Carl Hunzike was arrested on Aug. 24 inside North Korea after he crossed the Amnok River.
KCNA did not say why it took more than a month to announce the arrest and did not provide further details of the man, other than to say he worked for South Korean intelligence.
A spokesman at the U.S. embassy in Seoul said earlier: "We're trying to determine if he's a U.S. citizen. As far as I'm aware, this hasn't been determined yet."
A spokesman for South Korea's Agency for National Security Planning said: "We've never heard of the name. The allegation was made up by the North."
